transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
>> Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
Federal agents searched the home of Representative Ilhan Omar
this morning in the Washington, D.C. area.
That's according to reports from the Associated Press.
NPR's Lou Garrett says the Minnesota Democrat
has long earned the ire of President Trump.
>> In response to questions regarding the search
of Congresswoman Omar's home,
the Department of Justice tells NPR agents
with the Homeland Security Investigations, quote,
"executed a judicially authorized search warrant."
This warrant was approved by the DOJ,
and the search was done in Washington, D.C.
The DOJ says the HSI search was part of a, quote,
"ongoing federal criminal investigation."
NPR has reached out to Omar's office for a response.
The Minnesota representative was first elected to the House in 2018.
She's part of a group of progressive female lawmakers
known as the Squad.
Trump has long criticized Omar and the Squad.
Lou Garrett, NPR News, Washington.
>> Another attack on Riyadh's international airport
in Saudi Arabia has left one person dead
and 11 others injured.
It comes a day after a missile strike on a passenger terminal
that killed 13 people and wounded more than 300.
NPR's Aya Batrawi reports Yemen's Houthi rebels
claim responsibility for the first attack.
>> Riyadh airport has been hit at least four times
over the past week, including twice over the weekend.
The deadliest attack was Saturday.
The Houthis struck a passenger terminal there.
The Saudis released CCTV footage showing passengers,
many of the Muslim pilgrims headed to Mecca,
standing in line when a fireball hits the passenger terminal
and parts of the ceiling collapse.
Helicopters were seen flying into Medevac, the wounded out,
and Saudi authorities say 13 people of various nationalities
were killed, including a U.S. citizen.
>> NPR's Aya Batrawi reporting from Dubai.
>> Waves are pounding the shore in Long Beach, California
in the wake of tropical storm Rachel.
Steve Futterman reports damage assessments are underway
with dangerous surf expected to affect parts
of Southern California over the next few days.
>> Coastal areas suffered most of the damage,
high tides and powerful waves, battered beach cities,
including Long Beach, Newport Beach,
and in the San Diego area, Imperial Beach.
Some oceanfront homes were hit very hard.
The boardwalk in Long Beach suffered significant damage.
Many streets were flooded.
In some cases, drivers had to be rescued from their cars.
There were similar reports of damage to the South
in Baja, California.
This could be a preview of things to come,
as forecasters predict a very strong El Nino weather pattern
during the upcoming months,
which will bring additional powerful storms.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman in Los Angeles.
>> On Wall Street, the Dow was up 246 points.
This is NPR News.
The Nobel Prize in Economics is being shared by two Americans,
Robert Hall of Stanford University
and Michael Woodford of Columbia University
study how decisions by households
and businesses shape the economy.
Hall's research examines how spending
and hiring impacts recessions and recoveries.
Woodford's work explains how central banks
can use interest rates to keep inflation in check.
Protests are flaring again today in New Delhi,
despite the government banning demonstrations.
NPR's Dia Hadid reports thousands of people outraged
about revised voter rolls have been detained in recent weeks.
>> Hundreds of protesters gathered near the porticoes
of an upmarket shopping area,
chanting against the commissioner and the prime minister.
>> Not about the high, high, high.
>> Authorities dispatched thousands of police to downtown Delhi,
cut the Internet in parts of the city, diverted traffic,
and shuttered some metro stations.
That's been ongoing since Friday,
when a youth-led movement announced protests
to demand India's election commissioner resign.
Critics accuse the commissioner of overseeing
a revision of voter rolls that's disenfranchised
tens of millions of citizens.
The election commission says it works with complete integrity.
Dia Hadid, NPR News, New Delhi.
>> Pope Leo will undergo surgery this week
to remove a small growth from his lung.
The pontiff says doctors found the nodule
during recent medical checks and detected it at an early stage.
The Vatican says his recovery is expected to take about a week.
This is NPR.

topics.text: Federal agents search Representative Ilhan Omar's home in Washington, D.C. area in ongoing criminal investigation
Second Saudi Riyadh airport attack kills one and injures 11; Houthis claim responsibility
Tropical Storm Rachel waves damage Long Beach and Southern California coastal areas, rescuing drivers
Nobel Prize in Economics shared by Robert Hall of Stanford and Michael Woodford of Columbia
Protesters in New Delhi defy ban, demanding election commissioner resign over voter roll revisions
Pope Leo to undergo surgery this week to remove small lung nodule found early
